notes: v8 = v7 with one universe change (2026-11-17 14:30 UTC review): a token can be traded from 1 day after launch, was 3 hours (universe.min_age_days 0.125 to 1). Why: the test written on 16 Nov, when the 3-hour floor went in at Ajeeb's request, was met. It said to raise the floor, to 1 day first, if one day's trades on young tokens cost more than 5% of equity. On 17 Nov the four trades on tokens under a day old (GTA, LEOSTAR, BAWSAQ, bul; 9 to 16 hours old) cost 0.2523 SOL, 5.6% of the day's starting equity. Two of their three stops filled at -28% and -24% on price against a 12% level with every cycle on time, BAWSAQ was 88% under the buy price 30 minutes after the buy, and LEOSTAR fell 78% in one cycle ten minutes after the bot sold it. On the recorded snapshots the entry rules' first signals on tokens under a day old made -20.9% (13 on 8 tokens, 6 of them worse than -25%) against +4.6% at 1 to 3 days (11 on 4 tokens) and +4.4% at 3 days or more (29 on 8). Hints, on one bad day and few tokens; it is a risk limit, not a claim about returns. Tokens 1 to 3 days old stay tradable and are still judged apart. What the floor blocks stays measurable: python3 -m bot.replay --set universe.min_age_days=0.125. v7 = v6 with exit.trailing_stop_pct 10 to 5 (2026-11-16 22:30 UTC review: with one price every 5 minutes the half kept after the first target was sold far under a 10% trail level). v6 = v5 with universe.min_age_days 3 to 0.125, at Ajeeb's request on 2026-11-16 (his hypothesis: the volume in young tokens is genuine). v5 = v4 with entry.min_txns_h1 150 to 300 (2026-11-16 06:30 UTC review; a signal on a thinly traded token has been reliably bad). Entry is unchanged since v5, exit since v7; portfolio, safety, costs and discovery since v4. See reviews/LESSONS.md for the evidence and what would prove each change wrong. Every threshold is still an untested guess. Change one section at a time and bump 'version' on every edit so trades can be traced to the rules that produced them.
